title: UndoToast
summary: "Note deleted. Undo": a snackbar with an Undo action for a change the app already applied, whose result decides between undoing it and committing it.
whenToUse: For reversible, low-stakes actions the app applies at once, such as deleting or archiving one item, where a confirmation dialog would slow people down.
whenNotToUse: For destructive actions that cannot be reversed, confirm first with a dialog. For a message without an action, use a plain snackbar.
api: suspend fun SnackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message: String, actionLabel: String? = null, withDismissAction: Boolean = false, duration: SnackbarDuration = if (actionLabel == null) SnackbarDuration.Short else SnackbarDuration.Indefinite): SnackbarResult
@Composable fun MonarchSnackbarHost(hostState: SnackbarHostState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)

options.name: message
options.description: What just happened, in the past tense: "Note deleted".

options.name: duration
options.description: Use SnackbarDuration.Long (about 10 seconds) so the snackbar closes and the change commits; Material 3 extends it when an accessibility service needs more time.

states.name: ActionPerformed
states.description: The person pressed Undo: revert the change, then show a short "Restored" snackbar.

states.name: Dismissed
states.description: The snackbar timed out, was swiped away or dismissed: commit, for example run the deferred server delete.

appearance: A Material 3 snackbar in MonarchSnackbarHost: the inverse surface with the Undo action in the accent color for the inverse surface, 8dp corners. The same mapping in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web useUndoToast is a hook that commits when the toast closes for any reason and calls onUndo and onCommit at most once. On Android showSnackbar already suspends until the snackbar closes and says how: ActionPerformed or Dismissed, so the recipe is a when on the result and Monarch ships no API. The web countdown bar and undoAltText are not offered: a Material snackbar has no progress and its action is named by its label. A snackbar queued behind another waits rather than pushing it out; commit before showing the next one when that matters. When the coroutine is cancelled (the screen leaves), showSnackbar throws CancellationException; commit in the view model in that case. iOS composes MonarchToast with its own timer.
accessibility: The snackbar is a polite live region: TalkBack reads the message and the action when it appears.
The Undo action is a button with a 48dp touch target, and TalkBack offers it in the actions menu.
Material 3 keeps the snackbar on screen longer when an accessibility service asks for a longer timeout.
edgeCases: Showing a second undo snackbar while one is open queues it; the first still commits on its own result.
The person can swipe the snackbar away; that is Dismissed and commits.
